airtable.purpose: Find inventory rows at or below their reorder points in one selected base, table, formula filter, and result cap.
requirements: Connect the Airtable account that can read the chosen base and table.
Choose the exact base and table; `sample-warehouse-base` and `Inventory` are examples only.
Keep the formula filter and `max_records` bounded; the returned rows are not a complete inventory audit.
airtable.taskPrompt: Using the connected Weavz MCP server and the `inventory` Airtable alias, read the selected table rows that meet the supplied reorder filter. Identify rows where stock is at or below the reorder point and total units only across the returned rows. Cite each flagged row by its returned record ID. Example only: base `sample-warehouse-base`, table `Inventory`, returned IDs `air-row-1` through `air-row-5`; replace them with IDs returned by this account. Do not edit stock, create records, or infer supplier lead times.
airtable.readBoundary: `list_records` returns records from the chosen base/table, optionally filtered by an Airtable formula and capped by `max_records`. Work from the rows actually returned and report the cap; do not treat them as the full table or assume additional pages were read.
airtable.name: Airtable

asana.purpose: Review a bounded task sample from one Asana project, then inspect one selected task's details and notes.
requirements: Connect an Asana account that can view the selected workspace and project.
Supply the workspace and project identifiers; `sample-workspace` and `launch-project` are examples only.
Use only the returned task IDs and fields; do not assign, edit, or comment.
asana.taskPrompt: Using the connected Weavz MCP server and the `launch_tasks` Asana alias, summarize the selected project's returned tasks as completed, overdue, and upcoming, and flag missing assignees. Read the selected overdue task before describing its notes. Example only: workspace `sample-workspace`, project `launch-project`, task IDs `asana-task-1` through `asana-task-4`; replace with this user's IDs. State the as-of date and sample boundary. Do not assign owners, update tasks, or comment.
asana.readBoundary: `list_tasks` reads the named workspace/project and only the comma-separated `opt_fields` requested; this action has no page token input. `get_task` reads one exact task ID. Report absent fields as unknown and do not claim a complete project history.
asana.name: Asana

google-drive.purpose: Search a bounded Google Drive result page, then verify one selected file's metadata.
requirements: Connect a Google account with read access to the requested Drive files.
Provide a specific search query and use a returned `fileId` for metadata lookup.
`get_file` does not read the file body; open content only through an explicitly authorized content-reading tool.
google-drive.taskPrompt: Using the connected Weavz MCP server and the `project_drive` Google Drive alias, search only the supplied query and result page. Rank matching project documents with a short reason, then call `get_file` for one returned candidate and distinguish verified metadata from search-result summaries. Example only: query for release documents, page size 3, candidate IDs `drive-file-401` through `drive-file-403`. Replace these with returned IDs. Do not open or share unrelated files or imply that metadata search read document contents.
google-drive.readBoundary: `search_files` returns a result page controlled by `pageSize` and `pageToken`; it is search metadata, not document content. `get_file` fetches metadata for one exact `fileId`. Use only the requested page and state when a file body was not read.
google-drive.name: Google Drive

figma.purpose: Map a compact Figma file outline and inspect a small set of returned nodes for bounded design concerns.
requirements: Connect a Figma account with read access to the selected file.
Provide the exact file key or an HTTPS Figma file URL; choose node IDs from the returned outline.
Keep selected node IDs to 1–10 and depth to 1 or 2; this is REST design context, not Code Connect or native editing.
figma.taskPrompt: Using the connected Weavz MCP server and the `product_design` Figma alias, first read a compact outline for the selected file, then inspect only the selected returned node IDs. Report measured layout or accessibility properties separately from recommendations and cite returned node IDs. Example only: file key `sample-product-settings-file`, nodes `1:10,1:20`; use only IDs returned for the current file. Do not resolve an entire library, comment, or change the design.
figma.readBoundary: `get_file_outline` returns a compact tree capped by `maxNodes` (1–200); its expansion via `parentNodeId` is caller-directed, not API pagination. `get_node_design_context` accepts 1–10 selected nodes with depth 1 or 2 and returns bounded REST properties/reference IDs, not resolved libraries, Code Connect mappings, generated code, or expiring image assets. Request assets separately only when needed.
figma.name: Figma

storage.purpose: List files under one storage prefix and read selected UTF-8 research notes as a cited evidence notebook.
requirements: Connect to the intended Weavz workspace and end-user storage scope that contains the files.
Use the supplied prefix and exact paths returned under that prefix; `research/launch/` is an example only.
Use UTF-8 for text; use Base64 only when a selected file is binary. Do not write or delete files.
storage.taskPrompt: Using the connected Weavz MCP server and the `research_files` Filesystem alias, list only files under the selected research prefix and read the two requested note paths before summarizing their contents. Build an evidence notebook with findings, caveats, and source file IDs; distinguish statements in the notes from open questions. Example only: prefix `research/launch/`, paths `research/launch/experiment-brief.md` and `research/launch/interview-synthesis.md`, returned IDs `storage-exp-brief` and `storage-interviews`. Replace with current returned paths. Do not browse outside the prefix or write/delete files.
storage.readBoundary: `list_files` is filtered by `prefix` and returns paths in the current storage scope; it does not establish evidence outside that prefix. `read_file` returns the exact path's content as text or Base64 according to `outputEncoding`. Read only selected returned paths and avoid treating synthetic or user-provided notes as representative customer evidence.
storage.name: Filesystem

github.purpose: Review one selected pull request and a bounded sample of its returned file patches, keeping PR review distinct from issue search.
requirements: Connect a GitHub account or installation that can read the selected repository and pull request.
Provide an exact `owner/repository` and pull number; example repository `example-org/demo-api`, PR `42` is synthetic.
Use the read-only GET pull-files endpoint; do not create a review, comment, commit, or merge.
github.taskPrompt: Using the connected Weavz MCP server and the `code_review` GitHub alias, read the selected pull request and then retrieve its changed-file patches through the GET pull-files endpoint. Summarize behavior changes, test evidence, and concrete risks tied to returned paths. State if patches are missing or truncated; do not claim a full repository review. Example only: `example-org/demo-api` PR `42`, patch record IDs `pr-file-validator` and `pr-file-retry`; replace with this user's selected PR and returned files. This recipe reviews pull requests, not issue triage. Do not comment, submit a review, commit, or merge.
github.readBoundary: `get_pull_request` reads one exact repository/pull-number pair. `custom_api_call` should be limited to `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/files` with a bounded `per_page` query; inspect only returned patches, note missing/truncated patch text, and do not paginate unless the user explicitly requests more. This is not a general codebase scan.
github.name: GitHub

gmail.purpose: Search one bounded Gmail message page, read each selected message body, and separate explicit requests/deadlines from informational mail.

Prioritize explicit requests and dates, separating them from recommendations and informational updates. Example only: query `in:inbox newer_than:3d`, message IDs `gmail-msg-101` and `gmail-msg-102`; replace with returned IDs. Do not paginate, send, draft, or change labels.
gmail.readBoundary: `list_messages` returns message summaries from the selected Gmail query and page; `pageToken` is available but this task should not fetch additional pages. `get_message` reads one exact message and can return full content; attachment data is URL-safe Base64 and is not automatically interpreted. gmail.name: Gmail

google-calendar.purpose: Prepare one meeting briefing from a selected calendar event and a bounded related Gmail sample.
requirements: Connect a Google account with read access to the chosen calendar and event.

Use the `calendar` alias for event data; do not alter the event or invite attendees.

google-calendar.readBoundary: `list_events` is restricted by `calendarId`, time bounds, and `maxResults`; it may return a `pageToken`, but this task uses only the requested bounded page. `get_event` reads one exact event ID on that calendar. google-calendar.name: Google Calendar

notion.purpose: Find pages by title, retrieve selected page content, and answer only from the returned text.
requirements: Connect a Notion account that can read the chosen pages.
Search with title terms, then use the exact returned page/block ID as `parentId` to read content.

Cite the page IDs and distinguish source statements from synthesis. If the page is missing or its returned content is empty, say so. Do not edit pages or add comments.
notion.readBoundary: `find_page` returns a capped set of title matches (limit 1–100), not authoritative page text. For each selected result, call `getPageOrBlockChildren` with the returned `parentId`, `markdown: true`, and `dynamic: {}`. Report only content in the returned block tree; do not assume unreturned descendants or additional pages were read.
notion.name: Notion

google-sheets.purpose: Locate a spreadsheet, read one explicit A1 range by its actual spreadsheet ID, and separate closed-won rows from open pipeline.

google-sheets.taskPrompt: Using the connected Weavz MCP server and the `sales_sheet` Google Sheets alias, locate the requested spreadsheet if needed, then read only the user-selected spreadsheet ID and A1 range. Example only: spreadsheet ID `sample-fy26-regional-sales`, range `Deals!A1:F6`, rows `sales-row-2` through `sales-row-6`; replace with returned IDs. Do not write cells, include rows outside the range, or forecast from the sample.
google-sheets.readBoundary: `list_spreadsheets` returns a searchable file page; `read_range` reads only the exact `spreadsheetId` and A1 `range`. Keep closed-won and open values separate and do not treat the sample as an account-wide total.
google-sheets.name: Google Sheets

hubspot.purpose: Review the first bounded page of HubSpot deals using only selected stage, amount, pipeline, and close-date properties.

hubspot.name: HubSpot

salesforce.purpose: Build a short brief from Account records matching one explicit SOQL WHERE condition.

salesforce.readBoundary: `find_records_by_query` searches the specified Salesforce object using the supplied SOQL WHERE clause (omit the `WHERE` keyword). salesforce.name: Salesforce

linear.purpose: Search a bounded Linear issue sample and read one selected issue before recommending a review order.

linear.taskPrompt: Using the connected Weavz MCP server and the `project_issues` Linear alias, search with the selected project terms and a bounded result limit. linear.readBoundary: `search_issues` returns matches for the supplied query and `limit` (optionally scoped to a team). `get_issue` reads one exact returned Linear ID. linear.name: Linear

jira-cloud.purpose: Summarize the bounded issues returned by one JQL query for an active sprint, separating status, priority, blockers, and missing assignees.

jira-cloud.name: Jira Cloud

zendesk.purpose: Search one bounded page of open Zendesk tickets and read selected ticket details/comments for a safe handoff brief.
